notes: Eclipse Loop 1.9.0 Five things you asked for, and four things that were quietly broken. New Tap tempo. Tap the BPM readout in time with the music — two taps is enough, and each further tap refines it. It averages the last few taps rather than trusting the most recent one, so a single sloppy tap doesn't throw the tempo off. Double-click still types an exact BPM, and the wheel still nudges it (Shift for ±5). Works on the SEQ transport and on the Arrange window's clock. Chord palette. Right-click empty space in the piano roll and you get the chords of your key — triads and sevenths, named for what they actually are (Cm, E♭, Bdim, Fmaj7). Click one and it's written in at the beat and octave you clicked, one bar long, notes already selected so you can drag or trim straight away. One Cmd-Z removes the whole chord. Right-clicking a note still deletes it, as always. The chords are built from your scale rather than assuming major or minor, so the qualities are right in any scale — the vii of a major key comes out diminished, the III of a minor key comes out major, and Pentatonic or Blues give you a usable stack instead of a wrong one. Every note is in key
